title: Apple has $ 163 billion to burn, and Tim Cook plans to spend it - Nouvelles Du Monde
text:

Apple Inc. left things last month when it announced its plan to invest in the US economy, but the company was more than $ 160 billion of its own money. “Our current net cash position is $ 163 billion,” said Luca Maestri, Chief Financial Officer, said, “We are targeting net-cash neutral over-time. on the company’s earnings call . Live blog recap: Apple reports record earnings thanks to iPhone X sales Translated from corporate speak, that means Apple AAPL, + 0.21% plans to spend that $ 163 trillion in the last decade, when the company built up $ 284 trillion in cash reserves while using more than $ 100 trillion in debt to fund shareholder returns and other activities. Maestri said Apple would say more in its next quarterly report, when the company typically updates its shareholder-return plans . The bulk of that money will likely head back to investors. The company added $ 50 billion to its shareholder-return plan last year for buybacks and dividends, increasing its program to about $ 300 billion, and announced at $ 50 billion increase the year before, as well. Maestri said the company is typically 100% of its free cash flow to investors, “so that is the approach that we’re going to be taking.” Do not miss: Apple earnings show iPhone ‘supercycle’ is not happening, and that’s OK If Apple decided to double its annual rate, however, the company would still have $ 63 billion in net cash left to spend. There are a number of different ways that the company could use this money. Apple said in its January announcement that it would invest“over $ 10 billion” in data-center expansions . The company also set out to build a new campus and “create” 20,000 jobs – though it did not actually say it would hire 20,000 full-time Apple employees. 
Apple could also spend some of its net-cash balances to scoop up other companies. Speaking to this point on Apple’s earnings call, Maestri implied that Apple was not looking to change its strategy around acquisitions. “[/] Providing a new experience to customers,” he said, adding that “we are looking for” we will continue to do so. ” Apple made 19 acquisitions in 2017, Maestri noted, but all are thought to be smaller purchases, which has been Apple’s typical approach. The company’s largest acquisition to date, which it bought for $ 3 billion in 2014. Some have speculated that Apple might make a splashy move, buying Netflix Inc. NFLX, -1.93% Gold Walt Disney Co. DIS + 1.67% . See also: Netflix sees sharks approaching both sides in Apple and Disney Those are well worth $ 50 billion, though, with market values ​​of $ 115 trillion and $ 167 trillion, respectively, and that’s before factoring in the hefty premium one would have to pay to buy one of these giants. Apple will probably think smaller with its cash, looking for tuck-in acquisitions that add talent and give the company a base on which to build future product enhancements. Investors hungry for a piece of cash in the face of Thursday trading. The stock was already up 30.3% over the past 12 months, compared with a 31.6% gain for the Dow Jones Industrial Average DJIA, + 0.14% , of which Apple is a component. Related
